verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando ativelaṁ gihisaññattibahulo viharati.
verses.english: Now at that time Ānanda was spending too much time persuading lay people.

verses.pali: Atha kho yā tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā āyasmato ānandassa anukampikā atthakāmā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ saṁvejetukāmā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the deity haunting that forest had sympathy for Ānanda, wanting what’s best for him. So they approached him wanting to stir him up, and recited these verses:
“You’ve left for the jungle, the root of a tree,
having laid extinguishment in your heart.
What use is this hullabaloo to you?”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando tāya devatāya saṁvejito saṁvegamāpādīti.
verses.english: Impelled by that deity, Venerable Ānanda was struck with a sense of urgency.
